title.en: Stan’s limited angle

paragraphs.en: Stan is one of the four central boys and often provides a comparatively ordinary viewpoint amid the town’s absurd events. This edition borrows one narrow editorial angle: asking what a small shared activity actually needs. It does not claim you share his complete outlook, family, experiences or reactions to the show’s events. A choice for practicality can be useful without making other people’s imagination unreasonable.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦是四位核心男孩之一，常在小镇的荒诞事件中提供相对平常的视角。本版只取一个狭窄编辑角度：问小型共同活动真正需要什么。不主张你与他有完整相同的观点、家庭、经历或剧情反应。选择务实可以有用，也不代表别人的想象不合理。

title.en: The banner bigger than the meeting

paragraphs.en: Imagine a hobby club discussing an enormous banner for a gathering of six people. You ask where it would fit and what information the visitors need. Perhaps a small sign is enough; perhaps everyone enjoys making the huge one. The contribution is bringing the actual occasion into view before effort grows, rather than automatically choosing the smallest or least playful version.
paragraphs.zh: 比如兴趣小组为六人聚会讨论巨大横幅，你问放在哪里、来的人需要哪些信息。小标牌也许足够，大家也许就喜欢做大横幅。这个贡献是在投入变大前看见实际场合，并非自动选最小、最没趣的版本。

title.en: Practicality beside six other approaches

paragraphs.en: Kyle asks whether the agreed rules are consistent. Cartman makes a direct personal pitch, Kenny quietly handles a useful task, and Butters adds friendly imagination. Wendy checks whose voice or willingness is missing; Randy enjoys a grand optional idea. Stan’s angle asks what the occasion needs. You can use several of these contributions without discovering a hidden character or ranking which person is more sensible.
paragraphs.zh: 凯尔问约好的规则是否一致；卡特曼直接推介自己的想法；肯尼默默做好实事；巴特斯添友好想象；温迪检查遗漏的声音与意愿；兰迪喜欢宏大可选点子。斯坦角度问场合实际需要什么。几种贡献可以共用，不是隐藏角色，也不评谁更明智。

title.en: Make room for an enjoyable excess

paragraphs.en: A practical question can sound dismissive if the group mainly wants to enjoy making something together. Ask what people value about the elaborate version before reducing it. The extra decoration may itself be the activity. Conversely, you can state a genuine limit on your own time. A high count does not prove cynicism, emotional distance or superior common sense.
paragraphs.zh: 大家如果主要想享受一起制作，务实问题可能听起来像否定。缩减前先问复杂版本有什么让人喜欢，多出来的装饰也许本来就是活动。也可以说清自己的时间限制。高计数不证明愤世嫉俗、情感疏远或常识更高。

title.en: Try a purpose question

paragraphs.en: Before one small plan grows, ask what would make the occasion work for the people attending. Name one necessary part and one optional delight, then let the group choose how much effort to spend on each. Afterwards, compare what was actually used with what was enjoyable to make. This is a project observation, not a test of maturity or a duty to keep everyone realistic.
paragraphs.zh: 一次小计划扩大前，问怎样才适合参加的人。说出一个必需部分和一个可选乐趣，让小组决定各投多少。之后比较实际用到什么、制作什么很开心。这是在观察项目，不测成熟度，也不要求你负责让所有人现实。

title.en: Kyle’s limited angle

paragraphs.en: Kyle is one of the central boys and often questions the reasoning behind events around him. This edition selects a limited interest in consistent, understood agreements. It does not measure virtue, religious identity, intelligence or the accuracy of your opinions. Fictional disagreements can inspire a question about a hobby group without becoming a diagnosis or a claim that you are always right.
paragraphs.zh: 凯尔是核心男孩之一，常对周围事件的道理提出疑问。本版只选“规则一致且大家明白”的有限兴趣，不测美德、宗教身份、智力或观点正确性。虚构分歧可以启发兴趣小组里的一个问题，不变成诊断或“你总正确”的主张。

title.en: Two versions of a game instruction

paragraphs.en: Two friends interpret the same game instruction differently. You suggest agreeing on one interpretation before the next round, rather than deciding only after someone benefits. The agreement can also be a playful house rule, provided everyone understands it. Your role is to make the conditions discussable; winning the argument is not the only useful outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 两位朋友对同句游戏说明有不同理解，你建议下一轮前先约一种解释，不等有人获益才决定。也可以约好玩笑家规，只要大家明白。作用是让条件能够讨论，有用成果不只有赢下争论。

title.en: Consistency among other contributions

paragraphs.en: Stan checks what the activity needs, while Cartman states the version he personally wants. Kenny helps with setup and Butters proposes a friendly trial. Wendy asks whose participation is affected, and Randy imagines a bigger playful alternative. Kyle’s angle makes the common terms explicit. An equal count can preserve several full readings; none needs to become an inferior or supporting character.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦检查活动需要，卡特曼说自己想要的版本；肯尼帮准备，巴特斯提友好试玩；温迪问影响谁的参与；兰迪想更大的趣味替代。凯尔角度让共同条件明白。并列可保留几份完整读法，不必把谁降为次等或辅助角色。

title.en: An agreement can be revised openly

paragraphs.en: Consistency does not require keeping a rule that no longer works. Someone may need a different format or more time, and the group can agree to change the conditions before continuing. Ask whether a distinction has a relevant reason rather than assuming all differences are unfair. A high count cannot establish moral authority or permission to police other people’s choices.
paragraphs.zh: 一致不要求保留已经不合用的规则。有人也许需要不同形式或更多时间，小组可以继续前共同修改。先问区别有没有相关理由，不把所有不同都判作不公平。高计数不确立道德权威，也不授权监管别人选择。

title.en: Try stating the rule in one sentence

paragraphs.en: For one casual activity, ask each participant to describe the starting agreement in a sentence. Compare differences before play begins. If an exception is needed, say what changes and ask for agreement. Notice whether this makes the round easier to join. The exercise concerns a local arrangement, not a judgement about anyone’s honesty, ethics or political beliefs.
paragraphs.zh: 一次轻松活动前，请参与者各用一句话说起始约定，先比较差异再开始。需要例外时，说清改变什么并取得共同同意，观察是否更容易加入。这只关乎具体安排，不判断诚实、伦理或政治信念。

title.en: A deliberately narrow Cartman reading
title.zh: 刻意收窄的卡特曼读法

paragraphs.en: Cartman is one of the four central boys, and the story gives him many harmful actions. This guide does not recast those actions as strengths. It uses only an independently chosen, ordinary angle: directly presenting a personal preference in a low-stakes activity. Matching it neither attributes prejudice or cruelty to you nor endorses them. You can enjoy a fictional comparison while rejecting the character’s conduct.
paragraphs.zh: 卡特曼是四位核心男孩之一，作品里有许多伤害性行为。本说明不把这些行为改称优点，只独立取一个普通角度：在低风险活动里直接呈现个人偏好。匹配既不把偏见、残酷归给你，也不认可它们。可以接受人物联想，同时拒绝角色行为。

title.en: Pitching a tiny club theme

paragraphs.en: Friends need a theme for a craft afternoon, and you have a favourite. You state the idea, say why you would enjoy it and invite a decision. That is different from manipulating the vote or preventing others from speaking. A clear personal pitch gives the group useful information when it remains a proposal everyone can decline.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友要选手工下午主题，你有特别喜欢的一个。说清想法、为什么喜欢，再邀请决定。这与操纵投票或阻止别人发言不同。个人推介只要仍可被拒绝，就能给小组有用信息。

title.en: A preference within a shared decision
title.zh: 个人偏好进入共同决定

paragraphs.en: Stan asks what is workable; Kyle clarifies common rules. Kenny offers practical help, Butters makes room for friendly invention, Wendy checks willingness and quieter voices, and Randy suggests an extravagant option. Cartman’s selected angle makes one person’s desired choice visible. The group can combine those contributions. No count measures who deserves control, and this angle does not substitute for consent.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦问能否落地，凯尔约共同规则；肯尼出实事，巴特斯留友好想象，温迪确认意愿和安静声音，兰迪提夸张版本。卡特曼的选定角度让一个人的偏好可见。小组可结合这些贡献；次数不测谁应掌控，也不替代同意。

title.en: Be clear about where the pitch ends

paragraphs.en: A confident proposal needs a stopping point. Other people can choose differently, and you can decide whether you still want to participate. Explain a preference without implying that refusal is disloyal or foolish. A high count here does not mean selfishness, dominance, persuasive skill or a personality disorder. Neither confidence nor comedy makes a harmful demand acceptable.
paragraphs.zh: 明确提案需要有停止点。别人可以选不同版本，你也可以决定是否仍愿参加。说明偏好时，不把拒绝暗示成不忠或愚蠢。高计数不表示自私、支配、说服能力或人格障碍，自信和喜剧都不能让伤害要求合理。

title.en: Try a proposal with a real exit
title.zh: 试一个能被真正拒绝的提案

paragraphs.en: In a small group choice, say what you would like and one reason, then explicitly leave space for another suggestion. Listen without immediately repeating the pitch. Compare whether your preference was understood, even if it was not selected. This is a communication experiment, not a challenge to get your way or proof of a stable social style.
paragraphs.zh: 一次小组选择里，说想要什么、一个理由，再实际给另一提议留空间。听完，不急着重说。之后看看偏好是否被理解，即使没被选中。这是沟通尝试，不是设法如愿的挑战，也不证明固定社交风格。

Wendy checks people’s willingness and Randy expands an idea into a grand optional scene. Butters’s angle offers a friendly way in. These are editorial comparisons, not a hierarchy of seriousness, creativity or kindness, and you may recognise more than one contribution.

Notice which part made the activity easier to enter and whether anyone preferred another format. This is feedback on an invitation, not proof that you are naturally cheerful or have a particular learning style.

This edition takes one narrow editorial angle: checking whose voice, comfort or willingness a group decision has missed. title.en: A surprise that asks first

paragraphs.en: Friends plan to put one member in the spotlight as a surprise. You ask privately whether that person would enjoy the attention and offer a quieter version if they prefer it. The useful action is making a genuine choice possible before the plan is public. You need not announce that you know what everyone needs or turn a casual gathering into a public argument.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友想给某位成员聚光灯式惊喜，你私下问当事人喜不喜欢关注，也提供较安静版本。作用是在计划公开前给真实选择，不必宣布自己知道每个人需要，也不必把轻松聚会变成公开争论。

title.en: Participation alongside six other contributions

paragraphs.en: Stan asks what the event needs, Kyle makes the rule clear and Cartman names a personal preference. Kenny offers practical help, Butters invites playful participation and Randy imagines a grand optional version. Wendy’s angle checks whether people can choose comfortably. All can contribute to the same plan, and a full tie preserves the different readings without choosing a more virtuous winner.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦问活动需要，凯尔把规则讲清，卡特曼说个人偏好；肯尼做实事，巴特斯邀请轻松参与，兰迪想大阵仗可选版。温迪角度检查能否舒服地选择。都可贡献同一计划，全部并列会保留不同读法，不选更有美德的赢家。

title.en: Ask, rather than assume the answer

paragraphs.en: Someone quiet may be content to listen, want a written option or simply prefer to leave. Ask without turning the response into a performance. You can make an opening without demanding a contribution or claiming to know a hidden need. A high count does not prove empathy, activism or social competence; a low count does not establish indifference.
paragraphs.zh: 安静的人可能乐于听、想用文字，也可能想离开。询问时不让回应成为表演；可以开入口，不强迫贡献，也不自称知道隐藏需要。高计数不证明共情、行动主义或社交能力，低计数不确立冷漠。

title.en: Try one genuine choice of format
title.zh: 试一次真实的形式选择

paragraphs.en: Before one optional shared activity, offer two straightforward ways to participate and a clear way to skip. Ask privately if public attention is involved. Afterwards, check whether the choices were usable rather than counting how many people joined. The experiment concerns this invitation and context; it is not a test of your goodness or responsibility for everyone’s comfort.

The group might keep just one detail or enjoy the story without making anything. The contribution is opening a playful possibility. It does not need a real production schedule, a bigger budget or agreement to carry out every idea.
paragraphs.zh: 小组想一个小小虚构吉祥物，你喜欢编复杂背景、小冒险和戏剧开场。大家可能只留一个细节，也可能只听故事不制作。贡献是打开趣味可能，不必有正式制作日程、更多预算或实现每个想法的约定。

title.en: A large idea in a small group

paragraphs.en: Stan returns to what the occasion needs and Kyle asks which ideas become agreed tasks. Cartman states what he wants; Kenny offers a practical action. Butters makes an easy playful doorway and Wendy checks willingness. Randy’s selected angle stretches the imaginary version. These contributions can keep an idea enjoyable and optional, without assigning anyone a role for life or a score for creativity.
paragraphs.zh: 斯坦回到场合需要，凯尔问哪些点子变成共同任务；卡特曼说想要什么，肯尼做实际行动；巴特斯给轻松入口，温迪问意愿。兰迪角度把想象版拉大。几种贡献能让点子有趣且可选，不分派终生角色，也不给创造力打分。

title.en: Keep the imagined plan separate from a promise

paragraphs.en: Enthusiasm can make a playful suggestion sound like an assignment. Say which parts are only fun to imagine and what, if anything, you are offering to do. Ask before including someone else’s time or materials. A high count cannot establish recklessness, ambition or entrepreneurial talent. An elaborate joke also remains subject to the group’s comfort and consent.
paragraphs.zh: 热情会让趣味建议听起来像派活。说清哪些只是想着玩，哪些是自己愿做的，再问是否用到别人的时间材料。高计数不确立鲁莽、抱负或创业才能；复杂玩笑也要考虑小组舒适和同意。

title.en: Try a tiny version, or keep it imaginary
title.zh: 试小版本，或只留在想象

paragraphs.en: Describe one delightfully oversized hobby idea, then name a version that takes only a few minutes and is easy to decline. Let the group choose the tiny version, another idea or nothing. Notice whether shrinking the commitment keeps the imaginative pleasure. This is an experiment with an optional proposal, not a test of how bold you are or a reason to take practical risks.
paragraphs.zh: 说一个有趣夸张的兴趣点子，再找只需几分钟、容易拒绝的小版本。让小组选小版、另一个点子或都不做，观察承诺缩小后是否仍有想象乐趣。这是在试可选提案，不测胆量，也不构成实际冒险理由。

title.en: Twenty-one choices and every highest tie

paragraphs.en: Complete all 21 questions. Each choice explicitly adds one raw count to one of seven characters, for 21 counts in total. Every character is offered 12 times, three times in each option position. An absent option is not a rejection. Every highest count receives its full guide; all A produces three counts each and seven full guides. These are choice counts, not similarity percentages, moral scores, intelligence, diagnoses or population ranks. Small gaps have no established psychological significance.
paragraphs.zh: 完成21题，每个选择按明确映射为七位角色之一加1次，总和21。每位出现12次，四个位置各3次；当题没提供的角色不算被拒绝。最高计数全部保留完整说明；全A会各3次，七份全文一起呈现。次数不是相似百分比、道德分、智力、诊断或人群排名。微小差距没有已确立的心理意义。

title.zh: 原创同人版与来源边界
